dedupe_keys.name: syner g fragility functions and fragility function manager tool european elements at seismic risk

description: SYNER-G was an EU Seventh Framework research project, ending in 2013, on systemic seismic vulnerability and risk of buildings, transport and utility networks and critical facilities, with 14 partners from Europe, the USA and Japan. Its final report states that fragility curves were proposed for all elements at risk under the SYNER-G taxonomy, and that an open source Fragility Function Manager was built to store, harmonise, use and compare fragility functions for buildings and bridges. The Springer book edited from the project documents the typologies and fragility functions; its chapter by Silva, Crowley and Colombi says the manager stores, visualises and manages many fragility function sets and ships with a collection of European fragility functions as an electronic supplement. Coverage: European buildings, lifelines, transport networks and critical facilities under earthquake shaking. Access: through the book's electronic supplement. Licence: publisher terms. Caveats: the project ended in 2013 and its website is gone, so the supplement is the remaining distribution route. Simulation uses: choosing and harmonising fragility curves for systemic, multi-network seismic risk and cascading failure models. Related records: the ESRM20 European vulnerability database and the GEM global vulnerability model.
